summary: This configuration block adds security headers to responses for executable files like Perl scripts, PHP pages, and CGI programs. It tells browsers not to embed these pages in frames and to block cross-site scripting attempts, protecting against common web vulnerabilities.

explanations.1: FilesMatch uses a regular expression to match filenames ending in .pl, .php, .cgi, or .spl — these are typically executable server-side scripts.
explanations.2: IfModule checks whether the mod_headers Apache module is installed before trying to use the Header directive, so the config won't break if that module isn't available.
explanations.4: X-Frame-Options DENY prevents any website from loading this page inside an iframe or frame element, stopping clickjacking attacks.
explanations.5: X-XSS-Protection tells older browsers to detect and block reflected cross-site scripting attacks (the '1' enables it, 'mode=block' means block the page rather than just sanitize it).
